questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to inter-State river water disputes in India, consider the following statements:
1. Water supplies and irrigation are in the State List, subject to the Union's power to regulate inter-State rivers under the Union List.
2. Article 262 empowers Parliament to bar the jurisdiction of the Supreme Court in inter-State water disputes.
3. The River Boards Act, 1956 has been used to constitute several river boards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: No river board has ever been constituted under the River Boards Act, 1956. The Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956 provides for ad-hoc tribunals.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Inter-State River Water Disputes Act, 1956, consider the following statements:
1. Tribunal awards cannot be challenged before the Supreme Court under any provision.
2. The 2002 amendment mandated a limit of one year for setting up a tribunal.
3. The 2002 amendment mandated a limit of three years for the tribunal to deliver its award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Supreme Court has used Article 136 to hear appeals and modify awards, as in the Cauvery dispute in 2018. Article 131 covers original jurisdiction in disputes between States.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Tungabhadra river, consider the following statements:
1. It is formed by the confluence of the Tunga and the Bhadra.
2. It joins the Krishna as a right bank tributary.
3. Hampi, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, lies on its banks.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The ancient name of the river is Pampa and the Tungabhadra Board oversees water regulation. The Centre plans a high-level committee for the Telangana, Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka dispute.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's role in inter-State water disputes, consider the following statements:
1. Disputes about dam safety such as in the Mullaperiyar case are not strictly water disputes under the ISRWD Act.
2. The Mullaperiyar dam is located on the Cauvery river.
3. The Cauvery award was modified by the Supreme Court in 2018 and it directed the constitution of the Cauvery River Management Board.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Mullaperiyar dam is on the Periyar river in Kerala and operated by Tamil Nadu.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the proposed reforms for inter-State river water disputes, consider the following statements:
1. The ISRWD (Amendment) Bill, 2019 proposes a single permanent tribunal with multiple benches.
2. It proposes a Dispute Resolution Committee for time-bound mediation before adjudication.
3. The Inter-State Council under Article 263 can be used for defusing tensions.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Australia's Murray-Darling Basin Authority is cited as an integrated basin model.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to a comparison between the parliamentary systems of India and the United Kingdom, consider the following statements:
1. India follows constitutional supremacy while the UK follows parliamentary sovereignty.
2. The UK has no anti-defection legislation.
3. In India a minister can continue for up to six months without being a Member of Parliament.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In India courts can strike down unconstitutional laws through judicial review, which UK courts cannot do for Acts of Parliament.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to DISHA 2.0 (Designing Innovative Solutions for Holistic Access to Justice), consider the following statements:
1. It is a Central Sector Scheme implemented by the Department of Justice.
2. It runs for five years from 1 April 2026 to 31 March 2031.
3. Tele-Law offers free pre-litigation advice through Common Service Centres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. VIDHI-Sanjeevani is a new centralised digital platform, and Nyaya Bandhu promotes pro bono legal services.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to recent judicial pronouncements on rights, consider the following statements:
1. The Supreme Court in SaveLIFE Foundation recognised the right to trauma care as part of Article 21.
2. The Delhi High Court recognised the right to be forgotten as a facet of the right to privacy under Article 21.
3. The Supreme Court held that the right to walk on safe footpaths flows only from Article 19(1)(a).
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The right to walk flows from Article 19(1)(d) freedom of movement and Article 21. De-indexing of names in court records cannot be used in cases against women, children or breach of public trust.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to proof of citizenship in India, consider the following statements:
1. The electoral roll is conclusive proof of citizenship.
2. A passport is primarily a travel document and not a conclusive proof of citizenship.
3. Aadhaar is an identity document and not proof of citizenship.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The electoral roll creates a presumption but is not conclusive, as held in Lal Babu Hussein v. Electoral Registration Officer (1995). Section 20 of the Passports Act allows passports to non-citizens in public interest.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, consider the following statements:
1. The 2020 amendment banned sub-granting of foreign contributions.
2. The 2020 amendment requires foreign contributions to be received in a designated Punjab National Bank account.
3. The 2020 amendment capped administrative expenses at 20%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The designated account is with the State Bank of India, New Delhi main branch. The newly proposed rules include activity-based and geography-based regulation of NGOs.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities, consider the following statements:
1. India ratified it in October 2007.
2. The RPwD Act, 2016 expanded the recognised disabilities from 7 to 21.
3. The Convention is a non-binding declaration.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The UNCRPD is a legally binding human rights treaty that came into force in 2008. COSP19 marked its 20th anniversary.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National e-Governance Service Delivery Assessment (NeSDA) 2025, consider the following statements:
1. It covers only Central Ministry portals.
2. It is a biennial assessment by the DARPG.
3. It is based on the Online Service Index of the UN e-Government Survey.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It covers State, UT, city and Central Ministry portals for G2C and G2B services.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Which article of the Constitution empowers Parliament to adjudicate inter-State water disputes by law and exclude the courts' jurisdiction?
questions.why: Article 131 is original jurisdiction, 136 is special leave, and 263 provides for the Inter-State Council.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Quadrilateral Security Dialogue (Quad), consider the following statements:
1. It originated from coordination of humanitarian assistance after the 2004 Indian Ocean tsunami.
2. It has a permanent secretariat and treaty obligations.
3. It was formally proposed in 2007 by Japanese Prime Minister Shinzo Abe and revived in 2017.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Quad is an informal strategic grouping without a permanent secretariat, treaty obligations or dedicated funding. Exercise Malabar involves the navies of all four members but is not formally a Quad exercise.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the outcomes of the 11th Quad Foreign Ministers' meeting held in New Delhi, consider the following statements:
1. The Quad Critical Minerals Initiative Framework is a 20 billion dollar initiative for mining, processing and recycling.
2. The Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration initially focuses on the Indian Ocean Region.
3. A Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission is to be hosted by Japan.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Coast Guard-led Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission is to be hosted by India, after the first mission from Palau to Guam. Cooperation on 6G standards was also announced.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to challenges faced by the Quad, consider the following statements:
1. AUKUS raises concerns about the dilution of interest in the Quad.
2. The US decision to restore the designation of US Pacific Command replaces the Indo-Pacific Command name adopted in 2018.
3. The Quad has six leader-level working groups including Climate, Cyber and Space.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Implementation of the Quad Partnership for Cable Connectivity and Resilience has been limited to a subsea cable in Palau.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to BRICS, consider the following statements:
1. BRICS has a permanent secretariat in Johannesburg.
2. The acronym BRIC was coined by Jim O'Neill in 2001.
3. The New Development Bank was established at the Fortaleza summit in 2014 with an initial authorised capital of 100 billion dollars.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: BRICS has no permanent secretariat. The Fortaleza Declaration also created the Contingent Reserve Arrangement of 100 billion dollars. NDB is headquartered in Shanghai.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the membership of BRICS, consider the following statements:
1. Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, the UAE and Indonesia are listed as new members.
2. Saudi Arabia has formally joined BRICS.
3. Indonesia is the first Southeast Asian member of BRICS.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Saudi Arabia has not yet taken a formal decision on membership. Partner countries include Belarus, Bolivia, Kazakhstan, Cuba, Malaysia, Nigeria, Thailand, Uganda, Uzbekistan and Vietnam.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 16th BRICS Agriculture Ministers' Meeting held at Indore, consider the following statements:
1. It was the first such meeting to include Partner Countries alongside Members.
2. The BRICS Indore Declaration was unanimously adopted.
3. A Global Forum on Farmers' Rights in Seed Systems is to be coordinated by the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers' Rights Authority.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. BRICS AGRIN covers agro-inputs and genetic resources, and a BRICS Network on Digital Agriculture is coordinated initially by IIT Delhi.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Globally Important Agricultural Heritage Systems (GIAHS), consider the following statements:
1. It is a designation of the Food and Agriculture Organization.
2. Kuttanad below-sea-level farming in Kerala is a GIAHS site.
3. Pampore saffron heritage in Jammu and Kashmir is a GIAHS site.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's third GIAHS site is Koraput traditional agriculture in Odisha.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to challenges for India within BRICS, consider the following statements:
1. Differences between members such as Iran and the UAE make consensus difficult.
2. China's push for Pakistan's membership could make BRICS China-centric.
3. India wants BRICS to remain an anti-western platform.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India seeks to ensure BRICS remains non-western and not anti-western. The deputy foreign ministers' and foreign ministers' meetings in April and May 2026 failed to build consensus.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-France Innovation Roadmap 2030, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted during the Indian Prime Minister's visit to Nice in June 2026.
2. It aligns with the 2026 India-France Year of Innovation.
3. It supports France's target of welcoming 30,000 Indian students by 2030.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Pillars cover trusted AI, academic mobility, technological sovereignty and health data; the Kanpur aeronautics campus is planned with MSDE.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the pillars of the India-France Innovation Roadmap 2030, consider the following statements:
1. It integrates India's Data Empowerment and Protection Architecture with French trusted data spaces.
2. It expands the 2018 Mutual Recognition of Qualifications framework to emerging technology domains.
3. It includes a pilot between ICMR and France's Health Data Hub.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The InnoXchange Bridge provides a startup corridor for reciprocal access to laboratories and investors.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the 2026 G7 Leaders' Summit, consider the following statements:
1. India is a permanent member of the G7.
2. It was held in Evian, France, and India attended as a partner country.
3. The Prime Minister of India said the world faces a shortage of trust rather than resources.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a G7 member; it was invited as a partner country. The summit discussed the IMF-World Bank 3-Pillar Approach for debt and liquidity challenges.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q: BRICS Indore Declaration's 'BRICS AGRIN' initiative is aimed at cooperation in:
opts: Grain trading and price discovery in member countries
Agricultural credit and crop insurance for farmers
Fertiliser subsidy coordination and trade finance
questions.why: AGRIN stands for Agro-Inputs, Genetic Resources and Information Network.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to critical and rare earth minerals, consider the following statements:
1. Rare earth elements are a group of 17 elements comprising scandium, yttrium and the 15 lanthanides.
2. According to the IEA, China controls only about 10% of rare earth processing and refining.
3. All rare earth minerals are critical minerals, but not all critical minerals are rare earths.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: China controls about 90% of rare earth processing and refining, produces 69% of rare earths and has 49% of reserves. The India-US framework aims to reduce dependence on China.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's critical minerals cooperation, consider the following statements:
1. The India-UK Critical Minerals Global Supply Chain Observatory is a joint initiative of TEXMiN, IIT (ISM) Dhanbad and the University of Cambridge.
2. It supports the goals of the National Critical Mineral Mission.
3. The India-US framework builds on the earlier Pax Silica and FORGE initiatives.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The observatory is a data-driven platform to monitor global critical mineral supply chains.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Myanmar relations, consider the following statements:
1. The Rupee-Kyat settlement mechanism was operationalised in 2024.
2. The Kaladan Multi-Modal Project and the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway are connectivity projects.
3. The India-Myanmar border is about 1,643 km long.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Myanmar lies at the confluence of Neighbourhood First, Act East and MAHASAGAR policies.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-Oman Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreement, consider the following statements:
1. Oman offered zero-duty access for 99.38% of India's exports by value.
2. India offered tariff liberalisation on 77.79% of tariff lines while protecting sectors like dairy, oilseeds and cereals.
3. Oman is India's largest trading partner in the Gulf.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Oman is India's second-largest trading partner in the Gulf with about 11 billion dollars of trade. Its ports at Sohar, Duqm and Salalah offer access to GCC and East African markets.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India-Venezuela relations, consider the following statements:
1. India's main imports from Venezuela are pharmaceuticals and cotton.
2. Bilateral trade was about 678.94 million dollars in FY 2025-26.
3. Venezuela emerged as the third largest oil supplier to India in May 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India imports crude oil, mineral waxes, iron and steel, aluminium and other metals from Venezuela, while pharmaceuticals and cotton are among India's exports.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC), consider the following statements:
1. It was announced during the G20 Summit in 2023 under India's presidency.
2. It was announced during the 2019 BRICS Summit.
3. It has an East Corridor linking India to the Arabian Gulf and a North Corridor from the Gulf to Europe.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was announced at the 2023 G20 in India. Signatories are India, the US, Saudi Arabia, the UAE, France, Germany, Italy and the EU; it is estimated to cut time by 40% and logistics cost by 30%.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC), consider the following statements:
1. It is the flagship project of the Belt and Road Initiative.
2. It connects Gwadar Port with Kashgar in Xinjiang.
3. India supports CPEC as it boosts regional connectivity.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India opposes CPEC because it passes through parts of Jammu and Kashmir under illegal occupation, violating India's sovereignty and territorial integrity.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Alliance for Human Rights, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched by the UN human rights office, OHCHR.
2. It runs up to the 80th anniversary of the Universal Declaration of Human Rights in 2028.
3. The Universal Declaration of Human Rights was adopted in 1948.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Its guiding principles are Imagine, Dialogue and Act.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Peace Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It is published by the Institute for Economics and Peace.
2. India ranked 127th among 163 countries.
3. It is based on 23 indicators across three domains.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Iceland ranked first for the 19th consecutive year and Russia ranked last.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to India's border passes and neighbouring river issues, consider the following statements:
1. Lipulekh Pass in Uttarakhand lies near the tri-junction of India, Nepal and China.
2. Shipki La in Himachal Pradesh and Nathu La in Sikkim are other trade passes with China.
3. The 1996 Ganga Water Sharing Treaty with Bangladesh is due to expire in December 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Bangladesh has approved construction of the Padma barrage in Rajbari district.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's middle class and consumption, consider the following statements:
1. The richest 10% in India hold less than 20% of national wealth.
2. The World Economic Forum projects that by 2036 the middle class and affluent consumers will account for 93% of spending.
3. India's GNI per capita must cross about 4,500 dollars to enter the World Bank's upper-middle-income category.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The World Inequality Report 2026 says the richest 10% hold about 65% of national wealth and the top 1% about 40%. Household debt rose to 45.5% of GDP by March 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to measures for India's middle class, consider the following statements:
1. Union Budget 2025-26 raised the zero-tax threshold to Rs 12 lakh under the new tax regime.
2. The SWAMIH fund aims at completing stalled affordable and mid-income housing projects.
3. PM MUDRA Yojana has disbursed over 57 crore loans by March 2026.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Unified Pension Scheme is effective since 2025, and over 86.51 lakh senior citizens aged 70 and above hold Ayushman Vay Vandana Cards.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Government Securities (G-Secs) in India, consider the following statements:
1. Treasury bills are issued by the Central Government in 91-day, 182-day and 364-day tenors.
2. State Governments issue both treasury bills and dated securities.
3. Treasury bills are zero-coupon securities issued at a discount.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: State Governments issue only dated securities known as State Development Loans. Cash Management Bills were introduced in 2010 for maturities under 91 days.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the risks of holding G-Secs, consider the following statements:
1. Market risk arises when interest rate changes cause prices to fluctuate.
2. Reinvestment risk arises when coupons must be reinvested at lower rates.
3. G-Secs carry a high risk of default.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: G-Secs carry practically no default risk and are called risk-free gilt-edged instruments. They are issued through RBI auctions on the E-Kuber platform.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Foreign Portfolio Investment, consider the following statements:
1. FPIs generally do not participate in the management of the companies in which they invest.
2. FPI is generally considered short-term in nature.
3. The Fully Accessible Route lets foreign investors invest in select G-Secs without the limits applicable under the General Route.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The overall limit for non-resident individuals in listed equity was proposed to rise from 10% to 24%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016, consider the following statements:
1. The Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process is designed for large corporates and must be completed in 330 days.
2. It was enacted on the recommendations of the Bankruptcy Law Reforms Committee chaired by T.K. Viswanathan.
3. The Committee of Creditors, made up of financial creditors, evaluates resolution plans.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pre-packaged insolvency is a hybrid framework for MSMEs to be completed in 120 days. The mandated CIRP limit is 330 days but actual resolution takes about 744 days.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the IBC Amendment Act, 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It introduces a Creditor-Initiated Insolvency Resolution Process as a hybrid out-of-court mechanism.
2. The NCLT must admit insolvency applications within 14 days of a default.
3. Liquidation must be completed within 180 days, extendable by a maximum of 90 days.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It also provides an enabling framework for cross-border and group insolvency, and strengthens the clean-slate principle.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the IBC's achievements and challenges, consider the following statements:
1. Gross NPAs of banks fell from 11.5% in FY18 to 2.3% in FY26.
2. The Insolvency and Bankruptcy Fund provided in the original Code remains unoperationalised.
3. The ED's powers under the PMLA to attach assets may conflict with the IBC's clean-slate principle.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. IBBI is the statutory regulator with a Chairperson, three ex-officio Central Government members, one ex-officio RBI member and five other members.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Asset Reconstruction Companies in India, consider the following statements:
1. The concept was proposed by the Narasimham Committee II (1998).
2. ARCs are registered with the RBI under Section 3 of the SARFAESI Act, 2002.
3. ARCIL was the first ARC, incorporated in 2002.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. There are 27 ARCs registered with the RBI in 2026 and NARCL was announced in the 2021-22 Budget.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the RBI (Asset Reconstruction Companies) Directions, 2025, consider the following statements:
1. The minimum Net Owned Fund is Rs 300 crore.
2. ARCs are allowed to raise money by way of deposits.
3. The Capital Adequacy Ratio must be 15% of risk-weighted assets.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: ARCs are prohibited from raising deposits. ARCs must hold at least 15% of the issued Security Receipts and resolve assets in 5 years, extendable up to 8 years.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the functioning of ARCs, consider the following statements:
1. ARCs issue Security Receipts to banks that are redeemable only when the ARC recovers the loan.
2. ARCs charge sellers a management fee of 1.5% to 2% of asset value annually.
3. Roughly 80% of ARC recoveries have come through operational revival of businesses.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: About 80% of recoveries have come through debt enforcement or liquidation, not revival. The Sudarshan Sen Committee (2021) recommended that ARCs sponsor SEBI-registered AIFs.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q: The National Asset Reconstruction Company Limited (NARCL) was set up to take over:
opts: Small retail loans of urban cooperative banks
Defaulted loans of NBFCs irrespective of size
Large, complex NPAs of public sector banks
Stressed assets of foreign banks operating in India
questions.why: It is registered with the RBI as an ARC under the SARFAESI Act, with Canara Bank as sponsor.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Logistics Port Performance Index (LPPI), consider the following statements:
1. It is developed under the Sagar Aankalan framework.
2. It evaluates ports across dry bulk, liquid bulk and container cargo segments.
3. Mundra Port topped the container cargo segment among private ports.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Paradip topped dry bulk and Sikka Port and Terminals topped liquid bulk.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Hong Kong International Convention for ship recycling, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted under the International Maritime Organization.
2. It entered into force on 26 June 2025.
3. Alang-Sosiya in Gujarat accounts for nearly 98% of India's ship recycling.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India's share of global ship recycling rose from 30.1% in 2024 to 35.4% in 2025, and a ship recycling credit note of 40% of scrap value is offered.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's shipbuilding sector, consider the following statements:
1. Indian shipyards hold more than a 10% share of global shipbuilding.
2. Maritime India Vision 2030 aims at a 5% share of global shipbuilding by 2030.
3. The Maritime Development Fund has a corpus of Rs 25,000 crore.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India holds about 0.06% of the global shipbuilding market; China, Korea and Japan hold more than 90%. The Shipbuilding Development Scheme targets 4.5 million GT capacity.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to India's shipping and port sector, consider the following statements:
1. India is the second-largest supplier of seafarers globally.
2. Nearly 75% of India's transhipment cargo is handled at Indian ports.
3. Vizhinjam in Kerala is a semi-automated transhipment port.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: About 75% of India's transhipment cargo is handled at ports outside India. The Sagarmala programme was launched in 2015.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the legal reforms in the maritime sector, consider the following statements:
1. The Merchant Shipping Act, 2025 and the Coastal Shipping Act, 2025 have been enacted.
2. The Indian Ports Act, 2025 is among the new maritime legislations.
3. The Coastal Cargo Promotion Scheme aims to raise the modal share of coastal shipping and inland waterways from 6% to 12% by 2047.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The e-Navik platform supports India's commitment to the Maritime Labour Convention, 2006.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Kaushal Vikas Yojana, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2015 by the Ministry of Skill Development and Entrepreneurship.
2. The National Skill Development Corporation is its implementing agency.
3. The central and state components are split 50:50.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The scheme earmarks 75% of physical targets and financial allocations to NSDC and 25% to State Skill Development Missions. NSDC is a PPP with 49% government and 51% private shareholding.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the concerns raised by the Public Accounts Committee about PMKVY, consider the following statements:
1. Aadhaar Enabled Biometric Attendance System was fully implemented in the RPL component.
2. Only 1.10 crore candidates were certified against a target of 1.32 crore.
3. Only about 41% of trainees were placed.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: AEBAS was not implemented under the RPL component. Against the outlay of Rs 14,449 crore, Rs 10,194 crore was released and Rs 9,261 crore utilised.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the tourism sector in India, consider the following statements:
1. Tourism contributed about 5.22% of GDP in 2023-24.
2. India accounts for more than 10% of global international tourist arrivals.
3. India ranked 39th among 119 countries in the WEF Travel and Tourism Development Index 2024.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India accounts for less than 1.5% of global international tourist arrivals. It aims for 100 million inbound tourists and a 3 trillion dollar tourism economy by 2047.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to government initiatives in tourism, consider the following statements:
1. Swadesh Darshan was launched in 2014 and focuses on thematic circuits.
2. PRASHAD aims to upgrade pilgrimage sites.
3. Cruise Bharat Mission aims for 51 new cruise circuits.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. SASCI gives Rs 3,295.76 crore with 100% central funding for 40 iconic tourist centres.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the challenges of the tourism sector and the NITI Aayog report, consider the following statements:
1. A typical hotel project takes 36-48 months to become operational against 12-18 months in competing ASEAN destinations.
2. India's Visa Openness Index score of 38.14 is below the global average of 40.
3. Hotels need only a single approval in India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Hotels may require about 50 approvals and F&B establishments about 30 licences. The report proposes self-declaration for hotel classification and Entity Locker.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the ILO Convention No. 193 on decent work in the platform economy, consider the following statements:
1. It takes effect immediately upon adoption.
2. It is the first global treaty to set binding labour standards for gig work.
3. It was adopted at the 114th session of the ILO in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It takes effect 12 months after at least two member states ratify it.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the International Labour Organization, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1919 under the Treaty of Versailles.
2. It became the first specialised agency of the United Nations in 1946.
3. It was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize in 1969.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India has ratified six of the eight core ILO conventions and has not ratified the Freedom of Association and Right to Organise Convention.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the key features of the ILO Convention on decent work in the platform economy, consider the following statements:
1. It covers both online and location-based platform workers.
2. It allows platforms to withhold pay without any review.
3. Workers have the right to request a human review of significant automated decisions such as account deactivation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Workers must receive timely pay and, if considered employees, at least the minimum wage. Platforms must be transparent about automated monitoring systems.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the CAG report on State Finances 2024-25, consider the following statements:
1. Outstanding combined public debt of States was Rs 75.52 lakh crore, 23.27% of GSDP.
2. 18 States recorded fiscal deficits above the Fifteenth Finance Commission benchmark of 3% of GSDP.
3. Capital expenditure formed the major share of total expenditure of States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Revenue expenditure formed 83.41% of total expenditure and capital expenditure only 16.59%. The share of States in Union taxes rose from 27.73% to 31.76%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the new series of the Wholesale Price Index with base year 2022-23, consider the following statements:
1. It comprises 957 items in three major groups.
2. Manufactured Products have the highest weight.
3. The Producer Price Index is to replace the WPI in five years.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The first Output PPI, a trial Input PPI and a Service PPI for seven services were also released.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to District Domestic Product (DDP), consider the following statements:
1. The NSO guidelines use 2011-12 as the base year.
2. It is the district-level counterpart of GSDP.
3. It includes estimates of Gross District Domestic Product, Net District Domestic Product and per capita income.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The guidelines use 2022-23 as the base year. Approaches are income originating and income accruing.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the World Bank's Global Economic Prospects 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Global growth is projected to decline from 2.9% in 2025 to 2.5% in 2026.
2. The Strait of Hormuz disruptions raise energy prices and inflation.
3. South Asia remains the fastest-growing region.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. South Asia growth may moderate from 7.0% to 6.3% in 2026.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Development Policy Financing (DPF) of the World Bank, consider the following statements:
1. It can be extended as loans, credits or grants, or guarantees.
2. It is rapidly disbursed against policy and institutional reforms.
3. The World Bank approved a 1.5 billion dollar DPF for India.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Funds depend on adequate macroeconomic policy, satisfactory reform implementation and critical policy actions.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Hurun Global Unicorn Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India has 61 unicorns and slipped to 4th position.
2. Bengaluru is India's unicorn capital with 25 unicorns.
3. AI unicorns account for 36% of the total value of all unicorns.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The number of unicorns reached a record 1,603.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to SARTHAK-PDS, consider the following statements:
1. It integrates assistance for intra-State movement of foodgrains and FPS dealers' margin with the SMART PDS scheme.
2. Antyodaya Anna Yojana households are eligible for 5 kg of foodgrains per person per month.
3. It has an outlay of Rs 25,530 crore up to 31 March 2031.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: AAY households get 35 kg per family per month; Priority Households get 5 kg per person per month under the NFSA.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Smart Warehousing System of the Ministry of Consumer Affairs, Food and Public Distribution, consider the following statements:
1. It uses FASTag, ANPR and geo-tagged smart locks for gate automation.
2. It is being implemented in 215 warehouses of the Central Warehousing Corporation.
3. It is implemented only by the Food Corporation of India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: FCI is deploying it in 150 more warehouses; CWC warehouses are the first 215. About 60-70% of food grains are stored at household level.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to Muga silk, consider the following statements:
1. It is the world's only naturally golden silk.
2. It was the first silk to receive a GI tag in India.
3. Assam accounts for about 90% of the world's Muga silk production.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Antheraea assamensis silkworm feeds on Som and Soalu leaves, and Mission Senehjori targets 5 reeling units and 30 FPOs by 2028.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to seeds and pineapple in India, consider the following statements:
1. Pineapple is a true berry developed from a single flower.
2. The National Seed Reserve is an intervention under the National Food Security and Nutritional Mission.
3. Seeds in the reserve are produced through the SATHI portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The pineapple is botanically a multiple or composite fruit. Pineapple was declared the State Fruit of Tripura and Mission Queen Pineapple promotes the GI-tagged Queen variety.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the FAO's State of World Fisheries and Aquaculture 2026, consider the following statements:
1. Global aquatic animal production reached a record 235 million tonnes in 2024.
2. India is the largest aquaculture producer in the world.
3. India ranks second globally with about 9% of global aquatic animal production.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is the second-largest aquaculture producer, with 12% of global output. Sustainable fish stocks declined from 64.5% to 62.4%.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to FCNR(B) deposits, consider the following statements:
1. They can be opened by NRIs and OCIs.
2. They are term deposits for 1 to 5 years.
3. Both principal and interest are fully repatriable.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. FCNR(B) deposits are held in designated foreign currencies, protecting depositors from exchange rate risk.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to REITs and InvITs, consider the following statements:
1. REITs enable investors to earn from real estate without owning properties.
2. InvITs pool capital to own and operate infrastructure assets such as roads and telecom towers.
3. The RBI has allowed banks to lend directly to REITs and InvITs.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. REITs may be equity, mortgage or hybrid.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to the Zero Coupon Zero Principal (ZCZP) instrument, consider the following statements:
1. It is issued by not-for-profit organisations listed on the Social Stock Exchange.
2. It offers neither interest nor repayment of principal.
3. A company's CSR spending on ZCZP can exceed 10% of its total CSR expenditure.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Spending on ZCZP is capped at 10% of a company's total CSR expenditure in that financial year. It is regulated by SEBI.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to TReDS and CGSMFI-2.0, consider the following statements:
1. CGSMFI-2.0 gives the same 80% guarantee to all NBFC-MFIs.
2. TReDS is an electronic platform for financing trade receivables of MSMEs.
3. GeM has integrated TReDS as an additional payment mechanism.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: CGSMFI-2.0 gives 80% of default amount for small, 75% for medium and 70% for large NBFC-MFIs. It is sponsored by the Department of Financial Services.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to blockchain and the NPCI, consider the following statements:
1. Drunix is a private blockchain framework built by re-engineering Hyperledger Fabric.
2. NPCI is a not-for-profit company under the Companies Act, 2013.
3. Tokenisation converts ownership rights of real-world assets into digital tokens on blockchain.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. NPCI was initiated by the RBI and the Indian Banks' Association under the Payment and Settlement Systems Act, 2007.

questions.subject: Economy
questions.q:
With reference to new financial instruments and funds, consider the following statements:
1. Blue bonds earmark funds for ocean-friendly projects.
2. Seychelles launched the world's first sovereign blue bond in 2018.
3. The Price Stabilisation Fund for airlines is aimed at stabilising ATF prices.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The fund has a corpus of up to Rs 10,000 crore for 36 months; ATF accounts for nearly 40% of airline operating costs. Sagarmala Finance Corporation will launch India's first blue bonds.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to India's Ballistic Missile Defence programme, consider the following statements:
1. The programme was initiated by the DRDO in 1999.
2. Phase-I provided a shield against threats up to 2,000 km range.
3. Phase-III interceptors AD-AH and AD-AM target hypersonic glide vehicles and MIRVs.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. In June 2026 India completed Phase-II testing with AD-1 and AD-2 interceptors for 5,000 km-class threats.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the classification of India's ballistic missiles by range, consider the following statements:
1. Prithvi-II is a short-range missile with a range of about 350 km.
2. Agni-V is an intermediate-range missile with a range under 3,000 km.
3. Agni-II is a medium-range missile with a range of about 2,000 km.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Agni-V is classified as an intercontinental ballistic missile with range of 5,500-8,000 km. Agni-IV is intermediate-range with about 4,000 km.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Naval Anti-Ship Missile-Medium Range (NASM-MR), consider the following statements:
1. It is an indigenous all-weather over-the-horizon cruise missile.
2. It demonstrated low-level sea-skimming flight.
3. It was developed by the Hindustan Aeronautics Limited.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It was developed by the DRDO. It has pinpoint navigation and high terminal accuracy.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to technology integration in India's defence sector, consider the following statements:
1. The Defence Cyber Agency coordinates military space operations.
2. iDEX promotes defence innovation through startups, MSMEs and academia.
3. ADITI is an iDEX scheme giving grants of up to Rs 25 crore for critical technologies.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Defence Space Agency coordinates military space operations; the Defence Cyber Agency leads cyber defence. The Defence AI Council and Defence AI Project Agency lead AI efforts.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the High-Level Committee on Demographic Change, consider the following statements:
1. It is chaired by Justice P.P. Navlekar.
2. It includes the Registrar General of the Supreme Court as a member.
3. It is to recommend a time-bound mechanism for identification, detention and deportation of illegal immigrants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Members include the Census Commissioner and three others. The committee studies unnatural demographic change due to illegal immigration.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to illegal immigration in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Citizenship Act, 1955 defines an illegal migrant as a foreigner entering without valid documents or overstaying.
2. India has not signed the 1951 Refugee Convention.
3. The Immigration and Foreigners Act, 2025 explicitly distinguishes refugees from illegal immigrants.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2025 Act does not explicitly distinguish between refugees and illegal immigrants. It penalises illegal entry with up to 5 years' imprisonment, Rs 5 lakh fine, or both.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to judicial pronouncements on foreigners and refugees, consider the following statements:
1. In Mohammad Salimullah v. Union of India (2021) the Court allowed deportation of Rohingyas only after due process.
2. In NHRC v. State of Arunachal Pradesh (1996) the Court held that Article 21 protects foreigners from forcible eviction without due process.
3. The National Register of Citizens was implemented in Assam following Supreme Court orders.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Citizenship Amendment Act 2019 exempts six communities from Pakistan, Afghanistan and Bangladesh who entered before 31 December 2014.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the SIPRI Yearbook 2026, consider the following statements:
1. India is the largest arms importer in the world.
2. The world had about 12,187 nuclear warheads as of January 2026.
3. India's estimated warheads rose to 190.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is the second-largest arms importer with about 8% share, after Ukraine. Global military expenditure reached a record 2.9 trillion dollars in 2025.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Shangri-La Dialogue and BrahMos, consider the following statements:
1. The Shangri-La Dialogue is held annually in Singapore and organised by the IISS.
2. BrahMos is a supersonic cruise missile with a speed of Mach 2.8.
3. India signed a deal to supply BrahMos to Vietnam at the dialogue.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. BrahMos has stealth capability and a range of 290 km.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Netra AEW&C system, consider the following statements:
1. It is mounted on the Brazilian Embraer EMB-145I aircraft.
2. It was developed by HAL and inducted in 2005.
3. It has an AESA radar.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Netra was developed by DRDO's Centre for Airborne Systems; IOC was given in 2015 and it was inducted into the IAF in 2017. Final Operational Clearance was achieved now.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to recent military equipment in news, consider the following statements:
1. RudraM-II is an indigenous air-to-surface missile developed by the Research Centre Imarat.
2. LRLACM is the successor to the Nirbhay programme with a reported range of 1,000 km.
3. Su-57 is an American fifth-generation stealth fighter offered to India.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Su-57 is a Russian fifth-generation stealth aircraft offered by Russia. LRLACM's nodal laboratory is the Aeronautical Development Establishment, Bengaluru.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Khaan Quest exercise, consider the following statements:
1. It is conducted in Kazakhstan.
2. It started as a bilateral exercise between the USA and Mongolia in 2003.
3. From 2006 it became a multilateral peacekeeping exercise.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Khaan Quest is held in Mongolia.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to Access and Benefit Sharing (ABS) under the Nagoya Protocol, consider the following statements:
1. The Nagoya Protocol came into force in 2014 under the Convention on Biological Diversity.
2. Prior Informed Consent and Mutually Agreed Terms are key principles of ABS.
3. The ABS Clearing-House was established under Article 14 of the Protocol.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Cali Fund aims at benefit sharing from Digital Sequence Information on genetic resources.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to India's ABS framework under the Biological Diversity Act, 2002, consider the following statements:
1. It works through a three-tier system of the National Biodiversity Authority, State Biodiversity Boards and Biodiversity Management Committees.
2. The Biological Diversity (ABS) Regulations, 2025 exclude Digital Sequence Information.
3. Red Sanders accounted for the highest share of ABS realisation.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The 2025 Regulations replaced the 2014 rules and brought in Digital Sequence Information and benefit-sharing quanta based on annual turnover. ABS mobilised more than Rs 266 crore.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to benefit sharing examples in India, consider the following statements:
1. The Jeevani drug developed using Arogyapacha shared 50% of licence fee and royalty with the Kani tribe.
2. India successfully challenged foreign patents on turmeric and neem using historical documentation.
3. The Divya Pharmacy case of 2018 weakened the powers of State Biodiversity Boards.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Divya Pharmacy judgment affirmed domestic companies' benefit-sharing obligations and strengthened State Biodiversity Boards.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the International Treaty on Plant Genetic Resources for Food and Agriculture, consider the following statements:
1. Recipients of genetic resources can claim intellectual property rights over them.
2. It is administered by the FAO and entered into force in 2004.
3. It facilitates access to genetic material of 64 crops in its Multilateral System.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Treaty prevents recipients from claiming intellectual property rights. The Benefit Sharing Fund was set up in 2009 as its operational mechanism.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Stockholm Convention on Persistent Organic Pollutants, consider the following statements:
1. It entered into force in 2004.
2. India has accepted all amendments adding new POPs automatically.
3. POPs are toxic synthetic chemicals that resist degradation and bio-accumulate.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India ratified in 2006 using the opt-out clause, so new POPs do not automatically bind it. Aldrin, chlordane and DDT are examples.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Minamata Convention on Mercury, consider the following statements:
1. It was adopted in 2013 in Kumamoto, Japan and entered into force in 2017.
2. It bans new mercury mines and phases out existing mines.
3. It regulates artisanal and small-scale gold mining.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India is a party. PlanetGOLD is a GEF-supported programme for mercury-free gold extraction.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Global Environment Facility, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1991 and is the world's largest multilateral environmental financing mechanism.
2. The World Bank serves as its trustee.
3. It does not serve as the financial mechanism of the Stockholm Convention.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: GEF serves six conventions, including CBD, UNFCCC, Stockholm, Minamata, UNCCD and the BBNJ Agreement. It also administers the LDCF and SCCF.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to UNEP, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1972 after the Stockholm Conference.
2. It is headquartered in Nairobi.
3. UNEP launched the Global Chemicals Monitoring Programme with the GEF.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The programme is a 23.5 million dollar GEF initiative with 50 million dollars co-financing.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Bonn Climate Change Conference 2026 (SB64) and COP31, consider the following statements:
1. The UNFCCC is headquartered in Geneva.
2. SB64 is a key preparatory session for COP31.
3. COP31 is scheduled in Antalya, Turkiye from 9 to 20 November 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The UNFCCC is headquartered in Bonn, Germany. New 2035 goals include raising electricity's share of final energy demand to 35%.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Joint Crediting Mechanism between India and Japan, consider the following statements:
1. It is under Article 6 of the Paris Agreement.
2. It is India's first live bilateral carbon trading framework.
3. The Delhi Metro will be eligible for transfer of carbon credits under it.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. JCM is an initiative of Japan, with credited contributions counted toward both countries' NDCs.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the WMO Global Annual to Decadal Climate Update, consider the following statements:
1. It gives an 80% likelihood that the annual average global temperature will temporarily exceed 1.5 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels in at least one year.
2. It is issued every five years.
3. It gives an 86% chance that at least one year will be warmer than 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The report is issued annually by the WMO.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the WEF Energy Transition Index 2026, consider the following statements:
1. It tracks 120 countries.
2. Global energy transition readiness declined for the first time in over a decade.
3. India improved its rank to 70th.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Sweden, Finland and Denmark are top three. The Index uses 43 indicators on system performance and transition readiness.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to floating solar energy in India, consider the following statements:
1. MNRE estimated a floating solar potential of 102.18 GWp.
2. Maharashtra has the highest floating solar potential.
3. India's installed solar capacity increased from 2.8 GW in 2014 to 155 GW in 2026.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Madhya Pradesh and Karnataka follow Maharashtra, and the total assessed solar potential is 3,445 GWp.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to coal gasification in India, consider the following statements:
1. India's first commercial-scale coal-to-ammonium nitrate project is in Odisha.
2. It is being developed by a joint venture of BHEL and Coal India Limited.
3. The National Coal Gasification Mission aims to gasify 100 million tonnes of coal by 2030.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The project will produce 2,000 tonnes per day of ammonium nitrate, and India has a pilot underground coal gasification project in Jharkhand.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to methane and the Global Methane Pledge, consider the following statements:
1. The Global Methane Pledge aims to reduce methane emissions by at least 30% from 2020 levels by 2030.
2. India is a signatory to the Global Methane Pledge.
3. Methane remains in the atmosphere for about a decade, much shorter than CO2.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India is not a signatory to the Global Methane Pledge, which was launched in 2021 by the US and the EU. Methane is about 80 times more potent than CO2 over 20 years.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to the Jai Prakash Narayan Bird Sanctuary, consider the following statements:
1. It has been designated India's 100th Ramsar site.
2. It is an oxbow lake in Ballia district of Uttar Pradesh.
3. It lies in the Central Asian Flyway and is the wintering ground of migratory birds.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Also known as Surha Tal, it spans about 3,432 hectares, expanding to about 25,000 hectares in the monsoon.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to species in news, consider the following statements:
1. The hog deer is listed under Schedule I of the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972.
2. The caracal is found in Africa, Central Asia and south-west Asia and was spotted in Kuno National Park.
3. The Tapanuli orangutan is endemic to Sumatra and is Critically Endangered.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Tapanuli orangutan lives in the Batang Toru ecosystem and a 2025 cyclone killed about 7% of its population.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to corals, consider the following statements:
1. Corals belong to the group Cnidaria.
2. Zooxanthellae are symbiotic algae that give corals their colour.
3. Corals thrive in cold deep waters below 50 metres.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Corals thrive in warm, clear shallow waters generally less than 50 metres deep, at 23-29 degrees Celsius. The ZSI identified four sites for coral translocation in Great Nicobar.

questions.subject: Environment
questions.q:
With reference to marine conservation developments in India, consider the following statements:
1. The 3D-printed reef uses iron reinforcement for strength.
2. A giant Pavona clavus coral colony of about 4,250 sq. m. has been found near Kadmat Island in Lakshadweep.
3. Tamil Nadu will deploy India's first 3D-printed artificial reef under PMMSY.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The reef developed by Tvasta with ICAR-CMFRI uses no iron reinforcement and is highly porous.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to seismic doublets, consider the following statements:
1. Doublets are earthquakes of similar magnitude from distinct but closely related ruptures.
2. In a normal sequence, the largest quake is preceded by many aftershocks.
3. The first rupture can transfer stress to a nearby fault segment.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: In a typical sequence the larger quake is followed by smaller aftershocks. The western Venezuela doublet had magnitudes 7.2 and 7.5.

questions.subject: Geography
questions.q:
With reference to dam projects in news, consider the following statements:
1. The Kishau dam is proposed on the Tons river, a tributary of the Yamuna.
2. It is a roller compacted concrete gravity dam about 236 m high.
3. The Centre will provide 90% assistance for the water component.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Kirthai-II project is the third hydroelectric project on the Chenab to get approvals after the suspension of the Indus Water Treaty.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the recent global wave of youth protests, consider the following statements:
1. Such movements are often organisationally amorphous and mobilised through digital platforms without a prominent leadership.
2. The Carnegie Endowment's Global Protest Tracker records anti-government protests across many countries.
3. Sri Lanka's Aragalaya of 2022 was a cost-of-living protest.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Other protests cited include Bangladesh 2024 and Nepal 2025, and global youth unemployment stands at 13.0% as per ILO.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the way forward for youth discontent, consider the following statements:
1. The National Recruitment Agency is designed to conduct a Common Eligibility Test.
2. The Public Examinations (Prevention of Unfair Means) Act, 2024 provides deterrents for exam malpractice.
3. The National Youth Policy was adopted in 2014.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Second ARC recommendations on grievance redressal and CPGRAMS are cited as building blocks.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to India's digital health ecosystem, consider the following statements:
1. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission was launched in 2021.
2. The Healthcare Professionals Registry and the Health Facility Registry are part of ABDM.
3. The Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 provides consent-based protection of personal health data.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Over 90 crore ABHA accounts and over 100 crore linked health records have been created.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to digital health in India, consider the following statements:
1. The National Digital Health Blueprint was released in 2019 and emphasises a federated architecture.
2. U-WIN supports 11 regional languages.
3. The Telemedicine Practice Guidelines were issued in 2023.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Telemedicine Practice Guidelines were issued in 2020. PM-ABHIM has an outlay of Rs 64,180 crore.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Family Health Survey-6, consider the following statements:
1. Total fertility rate in NFHS-6 is 2.5.
2. It was conducted in 2023-24 with IIPS Mumbai as the nodal agency.
3. It covered 6.79 lakh households across 715 districts.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: TFR in both NFHS-5 and NFHS-6 is 2.0, below the replacement level. New indicators include digital literacy, DBT and SHG coverage.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to key findings of NFHS-6, consider the following statements:
1. Institutional deliveries rose from 88.6% to 90.6%.
2. The C-section rate declined from 21.5% to 18.0%.
3. Households covered under health insurance or financing schemes rose from 41.0% to 60.2%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: C-section deliveries rose from 21.5% to 27.2%, a public health concern. Full immunisation coverage rose from 83.8% to 87.1%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to child nutrition in NFHS-6, consider the following statements:
1. Stunting declined from 35.5% to 29.3%.
2. Severe wasting declined from 7.7% to 5.2%.
3. Underweight children declined sharply from 32.1% to 15%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Underweight children moved only marginally from 32.1% to 31.8%. Rotavirus vaccine coverage rose from 36.4% to 85.4%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to women's empowerment indicators in NFHS-6, consider the following statements:
1. Ever-married women experiencing spousal violence rose from 22.3% to 29.2%.
2. Women who have ever used the internet rose from 33.3% to 64.3%.
3. Women with a bank account that they themselves use rose from 78.6% to 89.0%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Spousal violence declined from 29.2% to 22.3%. Women married before 18 declined from 23.3% to 20.1%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to emerging health challenges in NFHS-6, consider the following statements:
1. Overweight or obese women rose from 24.0% to 30.7%.
2. Men with high blood sugar rose from 15.6% to 20.9%.
3. Tobacco use among men declined from 38.0% to 36.3%.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Overweight men rose from 22.9% to 27.3%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan, consider the following statements:
1. It provides free specialist antenatal care on the 9th of every month.
2. It targets pregnant women in their second and third trimesters.
3. Extended PMSMA was introduced in January 2022 to follow up high-risk pregnancies.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The scheme completed 10 years and private participants are honoured through the 'IPledgeFor9' awards.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to maternal health indicators in India, consider the following statements:
1. Maternal Mortality Ratio fell from 130 in SRS 2014-16 to 87 in SRS 2022-24.
2. India has achieved the National Health Policy 2017 target of MMR below 100.
3. Eight states have achieved the SDG target of MMR below 70.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. These states include Kerala, Maharashtra, Telangana, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, Jharkhand, Gujarat and Karnataka.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q: Pradhan Mantri Surakshit Matritva Abhiyan provides assured antenatal services on which day of every month?
questions.why: The fixed-day approach provides specialist-led antenatal care at public facilities.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Task Force on student mental health constituted by the Supreme Court, consider the following statements:
1. It was constituted in 2025 in the Amit Kumar v. Union of India case.
2. Student suicides were over 25% of total suicides in India as per NCRB 2022.
3. About 65% of institutes surveyed do not provide access to any mental health service providers.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Student suicides comprised 7.6% of total suicides in India (NCRB 2022). The Ministry of Health's Suicide Prevention Strategy (2022) was found to lack clear implementation guidelines.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the National Health Accounts estimates for 2022-23, consider the following statements:
1. Government health expenditure as a share of GDP rose from 1.15% to 1.43% between 2013-14 and 2022-23.
2. Out-of-pocket expenditure dropped from 64.2% to 43.4% of total health expenditure.
3. The estimates are prepared using the System of Health Accounts 2011 framework.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Social security expenditure on health rose from 6% to 9.9%.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Parliamentary Standing Committee report on teacher education, consider the following statements:
1. The ITEP curriculum was introduced by NCTE in IITs, NITs and Regional Institutes of Education.
2. A scheme of Rs 9,195 crore was launched to upgrade 613 DIETs as Centres of Excellence.
3. DIETs are monitored through the PRABANDH portal.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Committee's 380th Report also asked for filling faculty vacancies and integrating Anganwadi workers into teacher training.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Parliamentary Standing Committee report on higher education, consider the following statements:
1. Public expenditure on education was about 4.12% of GDP in 2021-22 against the NEP target of 6%.
2. Only 12 of 20 proposed Institutes of Eminence have been notified.
3. The Annual Survey on Higher Education has been published without any delay.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Three years of AISHE reports remain unpublished. The Committee also recommended a National Commission for Indian Knowledge Systems.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the Supreme Court's observations on human trafficking, consider the following statements:
1. It held trafficking to be rooted in Article 23 of the Constitution.
2. It held that consent is central in differentiating trafficking from voluntary adult sex work.
3. Essential elements of trafficking are Action, Means and Exploitation as per the Palermo Protocol.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Section 143 of the BNS defines trafficking and the BNSS makes it a cognizable and non-bailable offence.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the UNHCR Global Trends Report on forced displacement in 2025, consider the following statements:
1. India hosted the largest number of stateless Rohingya in the world.
2. 117.8 million people were forcibly displaced by the end of 2025, the first decline in a decade.
3. Rohingya remained the world's largest stateless population.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: India hosted 22,700 stateless Rohingya. India is not a party to the 1951 Convention or the 1967 Protocol.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the UNHCR, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1950 by the UN General Assembly.
2. It is financed mainly through assessed contributions of member states.
3. It is headquartered in Geneva.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: UNHCR is financed primarily through voluntary contributions from governments and private donors. It received Nobel Peace Prizes in 1954 and 1981.

questions.subject: IR
questions.q:
With reference to the international refugee protection framework, consider the following statements:
1. The 1951 Convention embodies the principle of non-refoulement.
2. The 1967 Protocol removed the temporal and geographical limits of the 1951 Convention.
3. The Global Compact on Refugees of 2018 is a legally binding treaty.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Global Compact on Refugees is a non-binding framework for responsibility-sharing. The 50 by 35 Initiative aims to halve refugee aid dependency by 2035.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Flex Fuel Vehicles (FFVs), consider the following statements:
1. Ethanol has a higher energy density per litre than petrol, so FFVs give better mileage on E100.
2. They can run on petrol, pure ethanol or any blend between them.
3. A fuel sensor detects the ethanol-to-petrol ratio and the engine control unit adjusts injection and ignition timing.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Ethanol has lower energy density than petrol, so vehicles on high blends have lower mileage. India recently gave legal recognition to E100 fuel.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to biofuels, consider the following statements:
1. Isobutanol is a four-carbon alcohol.
2. Isobutanol requires additional additives to blend uniformly with diesel.
3. India is likely to introduce blending of isobutanol with diesel.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Isobutanol blends uniformly with diesel without additives and has a higher energy content than ethanol. Brazil has an 80% flex-fuel fleet.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), consider the following statements:
1. BESS converts electrical energy into chemical energy during charging and reverses it during discharging.
2. Flow batteries store energy in liquid electrolytes kept in external tanks.
3. Sodium-based batteries described in the magazine operate at high temperatures above 300 degrees Celsius.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Vanadium redox flow and zinc-bromine batteries are examples of flow batteries.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the BESS ecosystem in India, consider the following statements:
1. The government has committed to deploying 47 GW of BESS by 2032.
2. The Viability Gap Funding Scheme supports 4,000 MWh of BESS by 2030-31.
3. Energy storage systems were included in the Harmonised Master List of Infrastructure in 2022.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. The Energy Storage Obligation by the Ministry of Power mandates a share of energy from storage. The Khavda project in Gujarat is 3.37 GWh.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the National Green Hydrogen Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in 2023 with an outlay of Rs 19,744 crore.
2. The SIGHT programme gives incentives for electrolyser manufacturing and green hydrogen production.
3. Green hydrogen is defined as hydrogen with emissions exceeding 5 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of hydrogen.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Green hydrogen is hydrogen with total emissions not exceeding 2 kg CO2 equivalent per kg of H2, averaged over 12 months. The mission is implemented by MNRE.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to green hydrogen, consider the following statements:
1. It is produced primarily by electrolysis of water using renewable power.
2. It can serve as a long-term energy storage medium.
3. It is odourless and colourless, which makes leak detection difficult.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is highly flammable and needs compression or cryogenic cooling because of low volumetric energy density.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's first hydrogen train, consider the following statements:
1. It was flagged off from Jind in Haryana under the 'Hydrogen for Heritage' project.
2. It runs on hydrogen fuel cell technology with water vapour as the only emission.
3. Germany's Coradia iLint was the world's first commercial hydrogen train, in 2018.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Lithium iron phosphate batteries supplement the fuel cell during acceleration and are recharged during braking.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the NITI Aayog roadmap on India's semiconductor industry, consider the following statements:
1. It has three pillars only: design, fabrication and packaging.
2. It envisions a 120-150 billion dollar domestic semiconductor value chain by 2035.
3. It aims to position India among the top three destinations for advanced packaging and OSAT.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It has five pillars: Pioneering, Policy and Investment, Production, People and Partnership. It seeks 135-180 billion dollars investment over the decade.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to India's semiconductor industry, consider the following statements:
1. India accounts for nearly 20% of the world's semiconductor design workforce.
2. India has 13 approved semiconductor projects operational or under development.
3. DHRUV64 and SHAKTI are indigenous processors.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. SPECS offers a 25% incentive on capital expenditure, and Gujarat's policy offers up to 30% capex subsidy.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to challenges in semiconductors, consider the following statements:
1. China has a dominant position in silicon, germanium and gallium among key critical minerals.
2. Fab units typically begin production within one year.
3. A modern analog fab typically needs over 5 billion dollars of capital.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Fab units typically need four to five years before production. Semiconductor manufacturing is also energy- and water-intensive.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The Green Hydrogen Certification Portal of India has been developed by which ministry?
opts: Ministry of New and Renewable Energy
Ministry of Petroleum and Natural Gas
questions.why: It facilitates certification under the Green Hydrogen Certification Scheme of India and SIGHT.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to synthetic biology, consider the following statements:
1. It involves redesigning organisms by engineering new abilities.
2. In synthetic biology scientists typically stitch long stretches of DNA into an organism's genome, while genome editing makes smaller changes to an organism's own DNA.
3. Engineering bacteria to deliver therapeutic agents directly to tumour cells is a possible application.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Concerns include biosafety, biosecurity, affordability and cyber-biosecurity.
