questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to IMI-resistant mustard hybrids, consider the following statements:
1. They are developed through mutation breeding and not through transgenic insertion.
2. A mutation alters the ALS enzyme so that imidazolinone herbicides cannot bind to it.
3. They help control the parasitic weed Orobanche.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. India imported about 16 million tonnes of edible oil worth nearly Rs 1.6 lakh crore in 2024-25.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to Smart Seed Coating technology and the SkyCast system, consider the following statements:
1. Smart seed coating was developed by ICAR-Indian Institute of Oilseeds Research using biodegradable biopolymers.
2. India became the 19th country to install the SkyCast System at Indira Gandhi International Airport.
3. SkyCast is based on the Winter Fog Experiment launched at Delhi airport in 2015.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. SkyCast integrates a Radar Wind Profiler, SODAR, Microwave Radiometer, fog aerosol spectrometer and a CL61 lidar ceilometer under Mission Mausam.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the James Webb Space Telescope, consider the following statements:
1. It observes the universe in the infrared spectrum.
2. It orbits at the Lagrange point L2, about 1.5 million km from Earth.
3. It is a purely NASA mission launched in 2021 from the United States.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is an international partnership of NASA, ESA and CSA, launched aboard an Ariane rocket from French Guiana. It detected methane on the interstellar comet 3I/ATLAS.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the human brainstem and ANCHOR, consider the following statements:
1. The brainstem connects the cerebrum only to the cerebellum.
2. ANCHOR is a 3D atlas of the human brainstem created by IIT Madras.
3. The brainstem is composed of the midbrain, pons and medulla oblongata.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The brainstem connects the cerebrum to the spinal cord and the cerebellum. It regulates breathing, heart rate, consciousness and sleep.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to fibre-optic drones and BGP hijacking, consider the following statements:
1. Fibre-optic drones use a physical fibre link instead of radio signals, making them difficult to jam.
2. BGP is the internet's routing system.
3. BGP hijacking involves falsely advertising a route to misdirect internet traffic.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. Fibre optics work on total internal reflection.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q:
With reference to the UN General Assembly Political Declaration on HIV/AIDS, consider the following statements:
1. It aims to end AIDS as a public health threat by 2030.
2. It excludes the elimination of mother-to-child transmission.
3. The 95-95-95 targets cover knowing status, accessing treatment and viral suppression.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It prioritises halting mother-to-child transmission, ending paediatric AIDS and dismantling stigma.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to the Harappan civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. The bronze Dancing Girl was found at Mohenjo-daro in 1926 in excavations led by John Marshall.
2. Harappan seals bore a pictographic script written in boustrophedon style, which is still not deciphered.
3. Harappans used iron extensively to make tools.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Harappans worked copper and made bronze by mixing tin; iron was not used extensively. The Priest-King sculpture is made of steatite.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to artefacts of the Harappan civilisation, consider the following statements:
1. The Pashupati seal was found at Lothal.
2. Fire altars were found at Kalibangan and Lothal.
3. Bead workshops existed at Chanhudaro and Lothal, and carnelian was used for beads.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The Pashupati seal was found at Mohenjo-daro and shows a three-faced deity surrounded by animals. A game board was found at Dholavira.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Gyan Bharatam Mission, consider the following statements:
1. It was announced in the Union Budget 2025-26 with an outlay of Rs 491.66 crore for 2025-2031.
2. It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
3. The National Mission for Manuscripts was restructured as the Gyan Bharatam Mission.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: It is a Central Sector Scheme. Kriti Sampada is the digital repository and Manus Granthavali is the software for uniform documentation.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to manuscripts in India, consider the following statements:
1. A manuscript is a handwritten composition at least 75 years old with historical, scientific or aesthetic value.
2. The Antiquities and Art Treasures Act, 1972 prohibits export of manuscripts over 75 years old by anyone other than the Central Government.
3. The Gilgit Manuscripts, India's oldest surviving manuscripts, are written on birch bark.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. UNESCO Memory of the World entries include the Rigveda manuscripts (2007) and the Natyashastra and Bhagavad Gita manuscripts (2025).

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to recently GI-tagged products, consider the following statements:
1. Kuchai silk of Jharkhand is a tussar silk produced on Asan and Arjun trees.
2. Khurasani Imli is the fruit of the baobab tree from Mandu in Madhya Pradesh.
3. The baobab tree is native to South America.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The baobab is native to Africa. It is a drought-resistant keystone species with a water-storing trunk.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Hiuen Tsang, consider the following statements:
1. He was a Chinese monk of the Han dynasty who visited India in the 1st century.
2. He visited the court of Harshavardhana.
3. He studied at Nalanda under Shilabhadra.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: He was a monk of the Tang period who travelled to India for 16 years between 629 and 645 CE. India and China are discussing joint UNESCO nomination of his travelogue.

questions.subject: History
questions.q:
With reference to Udant Martand, consider the following statements:
1. It is considered the first Hindi newspaper.
2. It was published from Calcutta in 1826.
3. Hindi Journalism Day is celebrated on 30 May to mark its first publication.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It was edited by Pandit Jugal Kishore Shukla and the name means 'the rising sun'.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q:
With reference to the Sangeet Natak Akademi, consider the following statements:
1. It was established in 1953.
2. It is an autonomous body under the Ministry of Culture.
3. It is registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. It is the apex national body for music, dance and drama, and its Chairman is appointed by the President.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the gallantry awards in India, consider the following statements:
1. Param Vir Chakra is the highest wartime gallantry award.
2. Peacetime gallantry awards were instituted on 26 January 1950.
3. Ashoka Chakra is the highest peacetime gallantry award.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Wartime awards were instituted on 26 January 1950 and peacetime awards on 4 January 1952, both with effect from 15 August 1947. Peacetime awards were renamed in 1967.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, consider the following statements:
1. It was launched in September 2018 as a Centrally Sponsored Scheme.
2. It is implemented by the National Health Authority in partnership with States and UTs.
3. It provides cashless cover of up to Rs 10 lakh per family per year.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: The cover is up to Rs 5 lakh per family per year. Senior citizens aged 70 and above get universal coverage via the Ayushman Vay Vandana Card.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to the coverage under PM-JAY, consider the following statements:
1. It covers pre-existing diseases only after a waiting period of three years.
2. It covers 12 crore economically vulnerable families, about 55 crore beneficiaries.
3. ASHAs, Anganwadi Workers and Anganwadi Helpers and their families are covered.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: Pre-existing diseases are covered from Day One. West Bengal joining brought nationwide coverage, and 1,961 packages across 27 specialities are covered.

questions.subject: Polity & Governance
questions.q:
With reference to Ayushman Bharat, consider the following statements:
1. Ayushman Arogya Mandirs provide comprehensive primary healthcare closer to communities.
2. The Ayushman Bharat Digital Mission creates an integrated digital health ecosystem through ABHA.
3. PM-ABHIM is meant to strengthen healthcare infrastructure and public health preparedness.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.why: All three are correct. These are the other three pillars alongside PM-JAY.

questions.subject: Art & Culture
questions.q: Hindi Journalism Day is observed on which date?
questions.why: It marks the first publication of Udant Martand in 1826.

questions.subject: Sci & Tech
questions.q: The interstellar comet in which the James Webb Space Telescope detected methane for the first time is:
questions.why: JWST observes in the infrared; the detection was reported in this magazine.
